name: Chubb Ltd.
reason: Best-in-class global commercial P&C underwriter under Evan Greenberg with a long record (adjusted EPS USD 9.76 in 2015 to 24.79 in 2025, 9.8% 10y CAGR, worst year -29.5% on 2017 cats, diluted shares down from 466m to 402m since the 2016 ACE-Chubb deal); passes the PGR/ORI long-record exception, but the deep dive must normalise hard-market-peak margins and higher investment yields (EPS 1.0x 10y max, consensus FY2 +4.2%, 2016-21 EPS only 10.12 to 12.56).

name: Investor AB
reason: Wallenberg investment holding company whose reported EPS (SEK 51.39 in 2025 vs -24.38 in 2022 and -0.73 in 2018) is mark-to-market on listed holdings and EQT, so earnings are set by equity markets rather than an operating business; consistent with INDU.A-SE, express via the underlying holdings instead.

name: Compagnie Financiere Tradition SA
reason: Viel & Cie-controlled interdealer broker with a good record (EPS CHF 5.35 in 2015 to 16.73 in 2025, 7/10 years >=7%) but revenue is set by rates/FX trading volumes and volatility (capital-markets activity), EBIT margin is at its 10y high of 14.4% vs 8.8% avg, and consensus LTG is only 4%.

name: Poste Italiane SpA
reason: Italian state-controlled (MEF/CDP ~65%) postal-financial group with steady EPS growth (EUR 0.42 in 2015 to 1.71 in 2025) but profits come mainly from BancoPosta deposit NII on Italian govies and Poste Vita, EBIT margin is at a 10y high (17.4% vs 9.0% avg), and payout and pricing are subject to government policy.

name: Brembo N.V.
reason: Premium brake maker whose adjusted EPS went nowhere in a decade (EUR 0.55 in 2015, 0.81 peak in 2017, 0.66 in 2025; 10y CAGR 1.8%) as EBIT margin fell from 12.9% to 7.5%; earnings tied to the auto production cycle and EV transition with acquisitions at 0.56x FCF.

name: Assicurazioni Generali S.p.A.
reason: Life-heavy multiline insurer whose adjusted EPS was flat at EUR ~1.38 from 2015 to 2019 and only rose to 2.85 in 2025 on rates and the P&C cycle, with 10y avg ROE 10.6%, ROIC 5.7%, consensus FY2-FY3 6-7% and persistent shareholder-control battles (Mediobanca/Delfin/Caltagirone); cheap-but-ordinary.

name: Barratt Redrow plc
reason: UK homebuilder with adjusted EPS falling from GBP 0.82 (FY2022) to 0.26 (FY2026), 10y EPS CAGR -7.2% and shares +3.6%/yr after the Redrow deal; earnings set by the UK housing/rate cycle (homebuilders are NO per the US standard).

name: Pennon Group Plc
reason: UK regulated water utility with adjusted EPS GBP 0.29 (2015) to 0.26 (FY2025) including a loss in FY2024, net debt/EBITDA 8.8x, shares +3.1%/yr, negative FCF and Ofwat/pollution-penalty regulatory risk; no route to 7% growth.

name: Inter Cars S.A.
reason: CEE auto-parts distributor with strong sales growth (PLN 4.8bn in 2015 to 21.2bn in 2025) and ROE ~15%, but GAAP EPS has stalled since the 2021 step-up (PLN 49.4 in 2021 to 57.1 in 2025), FCF was negative in 7 of 11 years and net debt rose from PLN 0.7bn to 3.7bn, so growth is working-capital and debt funded on a ~5% EBIT margin.

name: mBank SA
reason: Commerzbank-controlled Polish bank whose EPS fell from PLN 29.50 (2015) to losses in 2021-22 on CHF-mortgage legal provisions and then jumped to 103.54 in 2025 on peak NIM; 10y avg ROE 5.3% and Polish bank-tax/legal risk fail the bank standard.

name: Viohalco SA/NV
reason: Greek-family metals holding (aluminium, copper, cables, steel pipes, steel) with EPS EUR -0.27 (2015) to 1.03 (2022) to 0.19 (2023) to 0.91 (2025), 10y avg ROIC 3.9% and net debt/EBITDA 2.2x; earnings set by metal prices and project cycles.

name: Acea S.p.A.
reason: City-of-Rome-controlled multi-utility with adjusted EPS CAGR 5.8% (EUR 0.89 to 1.57), negative 10y FCF conversion, net debt/EBITDA 4.3x and consensus FY1-FY2 growth ~1%; regulated returns plus municipal control leave no route to 7% growth.

name: Bank Millennium SA
reason: BCP-controlled Polish bank with EPS PLN 0.49 (2015) to losses in 2021-22 on CHF-mortgage provisions and 0.99 in 2025 at peak NIM; 10y avg ROE 3.6% fails the bank standard.

name: Pandox AB
reason: Leveraged hotel-property owner (net debt/EBITDA 12x) whose EPS collapsed 75% in 2020 and whose growth came from acquisitions (3.4x FCF) and +2.6%/yr share issuance, with consensus FFO growth of -4.5% to +4.5%; hotel/property cycle with no route to 7%.

name: SSE PLC
reason: UK networks/renewables utility with adjusted EPS GBP 1.19 (FY2015) to 1.53 (FY2025), 10y CAGR 2.5%, negative FCF, net debt/EBITDA 3.8x and equity issuance; consensus 12-21% growth relies on regulated capex and wind/power prices, not a proven record.

name: STRABAG SE
reason: Austrian contractor with strong EPS growth (EUR 1.21 in 2015 to 7.94 in 2025) and net cash, but EBIT margin is at its 10y high of 4.9% vs 2.4% avg on a construction business with fixed-price project risk, consensus FY1 -1.2%, and the shareholder structure has been entangled in the sanctioned Deripaska/Rasperia stake.

name: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena S.p.A.
reason: Repeatedly bailed-out Italian bank (EPS loss of EUR 753.93 per share in 2016, shares +115%/yr over 10y via recapitalisations, 10y avg ROE -5.7%) still partly state-owned and now absorbing Mediobanca; fails every bank test.

name: Cembra Money Bank AG
reason: Swiss consumer-finance lender with steady but slow EPS growth (CHF 4.59 in 2015 to 6.20 in 2025, 10y CAGR 3.1%) and consensus LTG low single digits; credit-cycle lender with regulatory interest-rate caps and no route to 7% growth.

name: Swedish Logistic Property AB
reason: Young (2019) Swedish logistics-property owner whose GAAP EPS (SEK 1.15 to 4.16 to 1.55 to 2.78) is driven by property revaluations, with net debt/EBITDA 10.4x and negative NTM FCF; property and rate cycle with no FFO record.

name: National Grid PLC
reason: Regulated UK/US networks utility with adjusted EPS GBP 0.58 (FY2015) to 0.78 (FY2025), 10y CAGR 2.9%, shares +2.8%/yr including the 2024 GBP 7bn rights issue, net debt/EBITDA 6.0x and negative FCF; rate-base growth is equity-diluted so EPS growth has not reached 7%.
